column6: In physics , circular motion is a movement of an object along the circumference of a circle or rotation along a circular path.
column7: It can be uniform, with constant angular rate of rotation (and constant speed), or non-uniform with a changing rate of rotation.
column8: The rotation around a fixed axis of a three-dimensional body involves circular motion of its parts.
column9: The equations of motion describe the movement of the center of mass of a body.
column10: Examples of circular motion include: an artificial satellite orbiting the Earth at constant height, a stone which is tied to a rope and is being swung in circles, a car turning through a curve in a race track , an electron moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field , and a gear turning inside a mechanism.
column11: Since the object's velocity vector is constantly changing direction, the moving object is undergoing acceleration by a centripetal force in the direction of the center of rotation.
column12: Without this acceleration, the object would move in a straight line, according to Newton's laws of motion .

column21: In the United States, the title of federal judge usually means a judge appointed by the President of the United States and confirmed by the United States Senate pursuant to the Appointments Clause in Article II of the United States Constitution .
column22: In addition to the Supreme Court of the United States , whose existence and some aspects of whose jurisdiction are beyond the constitutional power of Congress to alter, acts of Congress have established 13 courts of appeals (also called "circuit courts") with appellate jurisdiction over different regions of the United States, and 94 United States district courts .
column23: Every judge appointed to such a court may be categorized as a federal judge; such positions include the Chief Justice and Associate Justices of the Supreme Court, Circuit Judges of the courts of appeals, and district judges of the United States district courts .
column24: All of these judges described thus far are referred to sometimes as "Article III judges" because they exercise the judicial power vested in the judicial branch of the federal government by Article III of the U.S. Constitution.
column25: In addition, judges of the Court of International Trade exercise judicial power pursuant to Article III.
column26: Other judges serving in the federal courts, including magistrate judges and bankruptcy judges , are also sometimes referred to as "federal judges"; however, they are neither appointed by the President nor confirmed by the Senate, and their power derives from Article I instead.
column27: See Article I and Article III tribunals .

column31: Variable Universal Life Insurance (often shortened to VUL) is a type of life insurance that builds a cash value.
column32: In a VUL, the cash value can be invested in a wide variety of separate accounts , similar to mutual funds , and the choice of which of the available separate accounts to use is entirely up to the contract owner.
column33: The 'variable' component in the name refers to this ability to invest in separate accounts whose values vary—they vary because they are invested in stock and/or bond markets.
column34: The 'universal' component in the name refers to the flexibility the owner has in making premium payments.
column35: The premiums can vary from nothing in a given month up to maximums defined by the Internal Revenue Code for life insurance.
column36: This flexibility is in contrast to whole life insurance that has fixed premium payments that typically cannot be missed without lapsing the policy (although one may exercise an Automatic Premium Loan feature, or surrender dividends to pay a Whole Life premium).
column37: Variable universal life is a type of permanent life insurance , because the death benefit will be paid if the insured dies any time as long as there is sufficient cash value to pay the costs of insurance in the policy.
column38: With most if not all VULs, unlike whole life, there is no endowment age (the age at which the cash value equals the death benefit amount, which for whole life is typically 100).
column39: This is yet another key advantage of VUL over Whole Life.
column40: With a typical whole life policy, the death benefit is limited to the face amount specified in the policy, and at endowment age, the face amount is all that is paid out.
column41: Thus with either death or endowment, the insurance company keeps any cash value built up over the years.
column42: However, some participating whole life policies offer riders which specify that any dividends paid on the policy be used to purchase "paid up additions" to the policy which increase both the cash value and the death benefit over time.
column43: If investments made in the separate accounts out-perform the general account of the insurance company, a higher rate-of-return can occur than the fixed rates-of-return typical for whole life.
column44: The combination over the years of no endowment age, continually increasing death benefit, and if a high rate-of-return is earned in the separate accounts of a VUL policy, this could result in higher value to the owner or beneficiary than that of a whole life policy with the same amounts of money paid in as premiums.

column54: Purdue University, located in West Lafayette, Indiana , is the flagship university of the six-campus Purdue University system .
column55: Purdue was founded on May 6, 1869, as a land-grant university when the Indiana General Assembly , taking advantage of the Morrill Act , accepted a donation of land and money from Lafayette businessman John Purdue to establish a college of science, technology, and agriculture in his name.
column56: The first classes were held on September 16, 1874, with six instructors and 39 students.
column57: Today, Purdue is a member of the Big Ten Conference , and is a well known world-class research institution.
column58: Purdue enrolls the second largest student body of any university in Indiana as well as the fourth largest international student population of any university in the United States.
column59: Purdue offers both undergraduate and graduate programs in over 211 major areas of study, and is well known for its competitive engineering curricula.
column60: The university has also been highly influential in America's history of aviation , having established the first college credit offered in flight training , the first four-year bachelor's degree in aviation, and the first university airport ( Purdue University Airport ).
column61: Purdue's aviation technology program remains one of the most competitive aviation-specific programs in the world.
column62: In the mid-20th century, Purdue's aviation program expanded to encompass advanced spaceflight technology giving rise to Purdue's nickname, Cradle of Astronauts.
column63: Twenty-three Purdue graduates have gone on to become astronauts, including Gus Grissom (one of the original Mercury Seven astronauts), Neil Armstrong (the first person to walk on the moon), and Eugene Cernan (the most recent person to walk on the moon).
column64: A sebaceous cyst () is a term that loosely refers to either epidermoid cysts (also known as epidermal cysts; L72.0 ) or pilar cysts (also known as trichilemmal cysts; L72.1 ).
column65: Because an epidermoid cyst originates in the epidermis and a pilar cyst originates from hair follicles , by definition, neither type of cyst is strictly a sebaceous cyst.
column66: The name is regarded as a misnomer as the fatty, white, semi-solid material in both of these cyst entities is not sebum , but keratin .
column67: Furthermore, under the microscope neither entity contains sebaceous glands .
column68: In practice, however, the terms are often used interchangeably.
column69: "True" sebaceous cysts are relatively rare and are known as steatocystomas or, if multiple, as steatocystoma multiplex .

column86: Harry Potter is a series of seven fantasy novels written by the British author J. K. Rowling .
column87: The books chronicle the adventures of a wizard , Harry Potter , and his friends Ronald Weasley and Hermione Granger , all of whom are students at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry .
column88: The main story arc concerns Harry's quest to overcome the Dark wizard Lord Voldemort , whose aims are to become immortal, conquer the wizarding world , subjugate non-magical people, and destroy all those who stand in his way, especially Harry Potter.
column89: Since the release of the first novel Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone on 30 June 1997, the books have gained immense popularity, critical acclaim and commercial success worldwide.
column90: The series has also had some share of criticism, including concern for the increasingly dark tone.
column91: , the book series has sold about 450 million copies, making it the best-selling book series in history , and has been translated into 67 languages .
column92: The last four books consecutively set records as the fastest-selling books in history.
column93: A series of many genres , including fantasy and coming of age (with elements of mystery , thriller , adventure , and romance ), it has many cultural meanings and references.
column94: According to Rowling, the main theme is death.
column95: There are also many other themes in the series, such as prejudice and corruption.
column96: The initial major publishers of the books were Bloomsbury in the United Kingdom and Scholastic Press in the United States.
column97: The books have since been published by many publishers worldwide.
column98: The books, with the seventh book split into two parts, have been made into an eight-part film series by Warner Bros. Pictures , the highest-grossing film series of all time.
column99: The series also originated much tie-in merchandise, making the Harry Potter brand worth in excess of $15 billion.
column100: Also due to the success of the books and films, Harry Potter has been used for a theme park, The Wizarding World of Harry Potter in Universal Parks & Resorts 's Islands of Adventure .
